title: GPS time
summary: GPS time synchronisation. Use a GPS receiver on USB or the UART as a time source when the box has no internet and no clock module. The toolkit has gpsd and the reference clock of chrony.
consent: gpsd listens for the receiver. It answers programs on the box only. gpsd keeps the position of the receiver while it runs. gpsd does not send the position to other devices.
notes: A box with no clock module starts with a clock that is hours behind. The clock doctor reports this. A receiver with a fix gives chrony the time to the second. If you connect the PPS pin of the receiver to a GPIO, the precision can be higher. pps-tools shows the pulses.

Put the refclock lines of chrony (SHM from gpsd, PPS from /dev/pps0) in /etc/chrony/conf.d. Chrony then also serves time to the hotspot (allow 192.168.4.0/24). The phones of guests can then agree with the certificate dates of the box.
gpsd is an exception to the rule that toolkit services stay stopped. It runs while the toolkit is installed. It starts when the receiver appears.
